items.title: New VOLTA Infostealer Uses Claude, Gemini, and Kimi AI to Rank Victims by Financial Value
items.snippet: Cybersecurity researchers have discovered a new Windows infostealer malware called VOLTA-AUTODOXER (aka VOLTA) that makes use of a large language model (LLM) to rank a victim's stolen data by their monetization value. Like other typical stealer families, VOLTA is equipped to harvest passwords and cookies from Chromium-based web browsers; data from Outlook profiles and Slack workspaces;
items.summary: A new Windows infostealer malware called VOLTA uses large language models like Claude and Gemini to rank stolen data by its monetization value. Windows users and system administrators are affected. Monitor endpoint security logs and maintain strong access controls.

items.title: Critical Langflow Flaws Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code on Servers
items.snippet: Two critical flaws in Langflow could let a remote attacker with no account bypass authentication or run arbitrary code, IBM said last week. Langflow is an open-source tool for building AI agents and workflows, and its vulnerability reports go to IBM. Every release from 1.0.0 through 1.12.8 has the flaws, and the only fix is version 1.13.0. Neither flaw is in CISA's Known
items.summary: Two critical flaws in Langflow versions 1.0.0 through 1.12.8 allow unauthenticated attackers to bypass authentication and execute arbitrary code on servers. AI workflow builders using Langflow are affected. Upgrade Langflow to the latest patched version or apply available workarounds immediately.

items.title: CVE-2026-119376 in SQLite
items.snippet: SQLite before 3.54.0 contains a stack exhaustion vulnerability that allows attackers to bypass the SQLITE_LIMIT_EXPR_DEPTH limit by chaining COLLATE postfix operators. Attackers can supply roughly 175,000 chained COLLATE operators in SQL or an untrusted database view to trigger unbounded recursion in sqlite3WalkExprNN() and crash the process.
items.summary: SQLite before 3.54.0 has a stack exhaustion vulnerability via chained COLLATE postfix operators allowing expression depth limit bypass. Applications embedding vulnerable SQLite versions are affected. Upgrade SQLite to 3.54.0 or later.

items.title: DBHub: MySQL and MariaDB comment interpretation bypasses read-only SQL validation
items.snippet: The read-only mode can be bypassed on the MySQL and MariaDB connectors. In read-only mode a caller can still execute arbitrary write and DDL statements (for example DROP TABLE), which defeats the protection that read-only mode is meant to provide when a database is exposed to an AI agent. Root cause The problem is a mismatch between how DBHub's SQL parser handles single-line comments and how MySQ…
items.summary: DBHub allows arbitrary write and DDL statements despite read-only mode in MySQL and MariaDB connectors, affecting database integrations exposed to AI agents. Upgrade @bytebase/dbhub to 0.22.6 or later.

items.title: SD JWT JS: Tampered disclosures silently dropped instead of rejected
items.snippet: When one Disclosure in an SD-JWT presentation is tampered so its digest no longer matches the Issuer-signed `_sd` array, `@sd-jwt/decode` 0.19.0 does not reject the presentation. It silently drops the unmatched Disclosure and returns a reduced claim set, reporting success. The Issuer signature is untouched and valid. This is a downgrade/omission primitive. A malicious or curious holder can presen…
items.summary: SD-JWT JS silently drops tampered disclosures and returns reduced claim sets instead of rejecting them, affecting applications using SD-JWT presentations. No fix yet: watch for a patch.
